newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police charge man after major arms haul.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police charge man after major arms haul.

text.p: Belgian police have seized eight tonnes of arms, ammunition and explosives -- including mortars -- in a raid on an arms dealer near the southern town of Mons.
Public Prosecutor Michel Bourlet told Reuters on Wednesday that arms dealer Marc Muller had been arrested and charged with gun-running and criminal association.

Speaking by telephone from the southern city of Neufchateau, he said the arrest and charges related to an attack on two gendarmes in the city of Bastogne in December 1995 by suspected members of the GIA armed Islamic movement.
"He has been charged with criminal association, illegal arms trading and possessing false documents," Bourlet said. "It is related to our GIA files."
"An operation like this is not set up in 24 hours. It has taken careful preparation," he said when asked why it had taken 15 months to link Muller to the attack.
Police and gendarmes spent Wednesday morning emptying a series of barns of their deadly hoard which included a field gun.
No comment was available from the Special Investigation Brigade in Mons that was coordinating the operation.
Newspapers and radio said French justice authorities had expressed an interest in the arms haul and Muller's links to GIA.
France has suffered several attacks over the past 18 months that have been attributed to Islamic fundamentalists.
